learn.hook: What if your teddy could talk? What would it say to you tonight?
points: The lesson 'Talking Toys' is about toys that come alive and talk to each other.
A make-believe story has things that cannot happen in real life, like toys that talk.
The characters in a story are the people, animals or things in it.
We learn about characters from what they say and do.

example.q:
Read:
At night, when everyone was asleep, the toys in Tara's room woke up.
'I am so bored of sitting on this shelf,' said Teddy.
'Let's have a race!' cried the little red car.
'Not so fast,' whispered the wooden horse. 'Tara is sleeping.'
So the toys played quietly until the sun came up.
Why did the wooden horse whisper?
steps: Find what the horse said: 'Tara is sleeping.'
If you speak loudly, a sleeping person may wake up.
So the horse whispered to let Tara sleep.
example.answer: Because Tara was sleeping and the horse did not want to wake her.

learn.reallife: When you play with your toys and give them voices, you are making your own talking-toy story!

games.title: Story order
games.prompt: Put the toy story in order
items: The horse asked them to be quiet.
The toys played quietly till morning.

games.title: True or false? (about the toy story)
items: The toys woke up at night.
The story says 'At night, when everyone was asleep, the toys ... woke up.'
Teddy was sitting on the shelf.
Teddy said, 'I am so bored of sitting on this shelf.'
The wooden horse wanted a race.
It was the little red car that wanted a race.
The story says they played quietly.
Toys talking is something that happens only in make-believe stories.
Real toys cannot talk by themselves.

quiz.q: The story says: 'At night, when everyone was asleep, the toys woke up.' When did the toys wake up?
quiz.explain: The story begins 'At night'.
quiz.mistake: Did not read the first words of the story

quiz.q: 'At night, when everyone was asleep, the toys in Tara's room woke up.' Whose room is it?
quiz.explain: The story says 'Tara's room'.
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the girl with the toys

quiz.q: 'I am so bored of sitting on this shelf,' said Teddy. Where was Teddy sitting?
quiz.explain: Teddy said he was sitting on the shelf.
quiz.mistake: Did not read what Teddy said

quiz.q: 'Let's have a race!' cried the little red car. Who wanted a race?
quiz.explain: The words 'cried the little red car' tell us the car said it.
quiz.mistake: Did not look at who spoke the words

quiz.q: 'Not so fast,' whispered the wooden horse. 'Tara is sleeping.' Why did the horse say this?
options: so that Tara would not wake up
quiz.explain: The horse knew Tara was sleeping and did not want to wake her.
quiz.mistake: Did not use the clue 'Tara is sleeping'

quiz.q: Teddy says, 'I am so bored.' What does 'bored' mean?
options: tired of having nothing fun to do
quiz.explain: When nothing fun is happening, we feel bored.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'bored'

quiz.q: In a story, toys wake up and talk at night. What kind of story is it?
quiz.explain: Toys cannot really talk, so it is make-believe.
quiz.mistake: Thinks everything in a story must be real

quiz.q: 'So the toys played quietly until the sun came up.' When did the toys stop playing?
quiz.explain: 'until the sun came up' means they stopped in the morning.
quiz.mistake: Does not understand the word 'until'

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Can toys really talk? What happened in Tara's room?'
teach.praise: So it's make-believe! I love stories where toys talk!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me if this story is real or make-believe, and what the toys did?

learn.hook: How do we know who is talking in a story? Look for the little marks around the words!
points: Dialogue means the words that characters say to each other.
Spoken words go inside inverted commas, also called speech marks: 'Let's play!'
Words like said, asked, replied, shouted and whispered tell us who speaks and how.
Read dialogue with feeling: softly for 'whispered', loudly for 'shouted'.

example.q: Read: "'Where is my ball?' asked Ravi." Who is speaking, and what did he say?
steps: Look at the words outside the inverted commas: 'asked Ravi'.
The words inside the marks are what he said: 'Where is my ball?'
example.answer: Ravi is speaking. He said, 'Where is my ball?'

learn.reallife: When you act in a class play, you read dialogue. Each character says their own lines.

games.title: Match the speaking word to its meaning

items.text: The words a character says go inside ___.

quiz.q: Read: "'Let's play!' said Mona." What did Mona say?
quiz.explain: The words inside the inverted commas are what Mona said.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the words outside the marks were spoken

quiz.q: What do we call the marks ' ' or " " around the words someone says?
quiz.explain: Inverted commas (speech marks) show the exact words a person says.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up speech marks with other marks

quiz.q: Read: "'Where is my kite?' asked Neha." Who is speaking?
quiz.explain: The words 'asked Neha' tell us Neha is speaking.
quiz.mistake: Looks only inside the speech marks to find the speaker

quiz.q: Which word means 'spoke very softly'?
quiz.explain: To whisper is to speak very softly.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up whispered and shouted

quiz.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
quiz.explain: Only the spoken words, 'I like cars,', go inside the inverted commas.
quiz.mistake: Puts the speech marks around the wrong words

quiz.q: Read: "'Help!' shouted the doll." How did the doll speak?
quiz.explain: 'shouted' means spoke very loudly.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'shouted'

quiz.q: Which word fits? "'What time is it?' ___ the clock."
quiz.explain: The words are a question, so the clock 'asked'.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that is not a speaking word

quiz.q: How should you read the words of a character who 'whispered'?
quiz.explain: A whisper is soft, so read those words softly.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the speaking word as a clue for reading aloud

teach.ask: Gappu reads a story but gets confused: 'How do I know which words someone said?'
teach.praise: The words inside the marks are what they said! I can read plays now!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what marks show spoken words, and which words tell us who is speaking?

learn.hook: 'My robot can dance.' 'Can your robot dance?' Spot the difference at the end!
points: A sentence begins with a capital letter.
A telling sentence tells us something. It ends with a full stop (.).
An asking sentence asks something. It ends with a question mark (?).
A sentence that shows a strong feeling ends with an exclamation mark (!): 'Wow, what a big kite!'
Names of people and places always begin with a capital letter.

example.q: Fix this sentence: 'where is my teddy'
steps: A sentence must begin with a capital letter, so 'where' becomes 'Where'.
It is asking something, so it is an asking sentence.
An asking sentence ends with a question mark.

learn.reallife: When you write a note to Dadi or a message on a card, capital letters and the right end marks make it easy to read.

games.title: Telling (.) or asking (?)
items: The ball is under the bed

games.title: Make a sentence
games.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence

quiz.q: Which mark ends an asking sentence?
quiz.explain: Asking sentences end with a question mark.
quiz.mistake: Ends every sentence with a full stop

quiz.q: Which of these is an asking sentence?
options: My teddy is on the bed.
quiz.explain: It asks something and ends with a question mark.
quiz.mistake: Does not see which sentence is a question

quiz.q: Which telling sentence is written correctly?
options: The doll is on the shelf.
the ball is under the bed.
The kite is in the sky
quiz.explain: It begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. The others miss a capital letter or a full stop.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the capital letter or the full stop

quiz.q: What does this sentence need? 'do you like toys'
options: a capital D and a question mark
quiz.explain: It must start with a capital letter, and it is a question, so it ends with '?'.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that questions need a question mark

quiz.q: Every sentence begins with a ___.
quiz.explain: We always begin a sentence with a capital letter.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up how a sentence begins and ends

quiz.q: Which mark ends this sentence? 'Wow, what a big kite'
quiz.explain: It shows a strong feeling of surprise, so it ends with '!'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it is a question because it has 'what'

quiz.q: Which of these must always begin with a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence?
quiz.explain: Names like Tara and Ravi always begin with a capital letter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only the first word of a sentence needs a capital

quiz.q: What is missing? 'The red car can go fast'
options: a question mark at the start
a capital letter at the end
a full stop at the end
quiz.explain: It is a telling sentence, so it needs a full stop at the end.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the missing end mark

teach.ask: Gappu writes 'can birds fly' and asks: 'Did I write it correctly?'
teach.praise: 'Can birds fly?' Yes, they can! I fixed it!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me how a sentence begins and which mark ends a question?
